enquiry: We would like an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to help us follow growth and notice changes earlier. Our team has mentioned both a biomass signal and a metabolic signal, but these have not been defined as separate targets. The broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops. We need help turning this request into an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today in the fermentation runs, and which decision should real-time data drive: when to feed, harvest, or intervene?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the decision the optical signal must support and therefore which signal matters first.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision unknown; the feasibility study will first test whether growth and metabolic changes are visible optically at all.

clarification_questions.question: Please define the biomass signal and the metabolic signal as separate targets: which variables (e.g. cell dry weight, viable cells, a specific metabolite or substrate) and at which levels, in ppm or %?
clarification_questions.why: Optical density tracks cell density but is not a viable cell count, and metabolic targets need a defined analyte or indicator; the choice of method depends on this.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Targets undefined and levels unknown; lab screening establishes whether the signals are ppm or % level before any method is chosen.

clarification_questions.question: At the measurement point, is the broth clear, turbid or opaque, and how does its optical density vary across the run and between batches?
clarification_questions.why: Optical properties determine the probe geometry (transmission, transflection, diffuse reflection or ATR).
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical properties unknown; lab screening on representative broth samples across the run establishes the probe geometry.

clarification_questions.question: What are the fermentation conditions (temperature, pressure, aeration, medium composition), are there gas bubbles or fouling, and how is the vessel cleaned or sterilised?
clarification_questions.why: Bubbles, fouling and sterilisation affect probe design, signal stability and the cleaning requirements for in-line use.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Conditions unknown; the lab trial records them and assumes an in-line probe must withstand the sterilisation used at the site.

clarification_questions.question: Where would the sensor be installed (vessel port, loop, sampling line), how far is the analyzer from that point, and do you have existing optical fibers?
clarification_questions.why: Distance and fiber type determine which wavelengths can reach the probe and whether remote measurement is feasible.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation and distance unknown; the feasibility study starts with a bench setup and no reuse of existing fibers.

clarification_questions.question: Which reference lab methods are used today for biomass and for the metabolic variables, and what are their accuracy and sampling frequency?
clarification_questions.why: Time-aligned reference data are needed to build and judge any optical model.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and accuracy unknown; the study defines reference measurements together with the client before data collection.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the optical measurement?
clarification_questions.why: These set the acceptable simplicity and cost of the sensor and whether a few-wavelength sensor or a broader lab system is appropriate.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the study proceeds with lab screening and does not set a performance target.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The cited DOCX §5 row says optical density is not a viable cell count, which is a general limitation; it does not mention yeast-specific calibration, so the claim's 'yeast-specific calibration is not shown' is not stated by the cited page, but the core statement is supported. The claim adds a yeast context not present in the cited source. Fix: Remove the yeast-specific clause or cite a page that discusses yeast calibration; keep only 'Optical density is not a viable cell count' as supported by DOCX §5.

overstated: S01 p.16 says Raman 'can be used' to provide a molecular fingerprint for direct detection of glucose, acetate, or lactate; the claim states it is used in a bioprocess example as established fact, which is more certain than the page's stated possibility. Fix: Rephrase as: Raman can be used for direct detection of glucose, acetate or lactate in a bioprocess setting, per the cited example.

overstated: S01 p.16 says UV/Vis 'can be deployed' as a low-cost tool for biomass monitoring because turbidity 'correlates well' with cell density; the claim says the example 'supports' it, which is stronger than a described possibility but the page does state correlation. The 'low-cost trend' wording is only partly supported. Fix: Say: S01 p.16 describes UV/Vis turbidity as a possible low-cost biomass monitoring approach, since turbidity correlates with cell density.

overstated: S01 p.16 describes Raman as a possible molecular fingerprint for these metabolites and notes it suits aqueous environments; 'supports' presents an illustrative example as established support. Fix: Rephrase to say the cited page describes Raman as usable for detecting these metabolites in aqueous media.

different_context: S01 p.11 says fluorescence superposition complicates Raman for many organic compounds in general; the claim applies it to the bioprocess context and adds a 'check signal quality first' recommendation not on the page. Fix: Limit to: S01 p.11 notes that luminescence (fluorescence) can overlap Raman bands for many organic compounds, and that specialized filters and probes can mitigate this.

not_supported: S01 p.7 and p.8 discuss synergy and multispectral analysis, but do not state that each method must be assessed alone first or that added value is a hypothesis to test. Fix: Rephrase to what the pages say, e.g. combinations can provide synergy for some problems, without asserting a testing procedure.

not_supported: The cited table rows list UV-Vis transmission/transflection probes for liquids (1-10 mm) and ATR probes with very short depth (0.1-1 um), but the table does not say to choose transmission for clear broth or ATR only when optical density saturates; that selection logic comes from S01 p.16 only in a general sense. Fix: Attribute the selection rule to S01 p.16 explicitly and treat the table rows as supporting path-length information only.

different_context: S02 p.6 gives the transmission range for standard and Al/Cu-coated UV-VIS silica fibers, but the claim applies it as a fiber for this link without a fiber-length or configuration caveat that the DOCX says is needed; the page itself is a figure transcription to be checked. Fix: State that the range is from S02 p.6 (figure transcription, check the figure) and that actual transmission depends on configuration and fiber length.

not_supported: S02 p.6 lists transmission ranges only; it does not state which fiber families are 'full range' or 'partial' for UV-Vis or Raman, so the rule check is not supported by the cited page. Fix: Remove the full/partial classification or cite a source that defines it; use S02 p.6 only for the transmission ranges.

not_supported: DOCX §5 lists calibration as matrix-specific and says calibration depends on the matrix, but does not explicitly say a change of medium, strain or formulation invalidates it. Fix: Rephrase: calibration is specific to the matrix, so changes in medium or formulation may require recalibration.

not_supported: S01 p.16 supports saturation with rising opacity and turbidity; S01 p.7 mentions process turbulence as a morphological factor but does not say bubbles or turbulence can mimic composition. Fix: Remove the bubble/turbulence mimicry claim or state only that process turbulence must be considered as a morphological factor (S01 p.7).

overstated: S01 p.7 and p.8 describe synergy as possible and a combination as sometimes solving problems, not a guarantee; the claim's 'neither ... is guaranteed' wording addresses detection speed, which the pages do not discuss at all. Fix: Remove the earlier-detection claim or state that the cited pages describe combinations as possibly beneficial without guaranteeing improved detection.

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
